case_name: Tamil Nadu Housing Board v L. Chandrasekaran and others
facts: The land of the respondents falling in Survey Nos.340, 341 and 343, Mogappair Village, Sedapet Taluk formed part of 513.52 acres acquired by the Government of Tamil Nadu for Ambattur Neighborhood Scheme.
Notification u/s.4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, 'the Act') was issued on 23.10.1975 and declaration u/s.6 was issued on 2.11.1978.
Some of the land owners including A.S. Naidu challenged the acquisition proceedings by filing writ petitions u/art.226 of the Constitution of India.

L. Chandrasekaran (respondent in Civil Appeal No.3148/2002) who had not challenged the acquisition proceedings filed a writ petition sometime in the year 1997 for issue of a direction to the appellant-Board to certify that the acquired land was no longer needed for the purpose for which it was acquired.
issues: Whether the Division Bench of the High Court committed serious error by issuing a mandamus for release of the acquired land ignoring that the same had been transferred to the appellant-Board and the latter had utilized the same for housing purposes.
Whether the respondents can take advantage of the quashing of acquisition proceedings in the case of A.S. Naidu and others.
petitioner_arguments: The Division Bench did not find any illegality in the decision taken by the Government or error in the orders passed by the learned Single Judge, but allowed the writ appeals by simply relying upon order dated 18.2.2000 passed in Writ Appeal No.2430/1999 and directed the appellant-Board to reconvey the land to the respondents subject to their depositing the amount of compensation together with interest.
respondent_arguments: The Government is empowered to decide whether the acquired land is no longer required for the purpose for which it was acquired or for any other public purpose and the decision taken in that regard cannot be nullified by the Court unless it is shown to be totally arbitrary or malafide.
court_reasoning: We have no doubt that if the appellants apply to the State for relief under Section 48-B of the Act, the State in due discharge of its official duty will consider the case of each of the petitioners/appellants on merits in accordance with law within three months from today and pass appropriate speaking orders.
holding: The Division Bench allowed the writ appeals by simply relying upon order dated 18.2.2000 passed in Writ Appeal No.2430/1999 and directed the appellant-Board to reconvey the land to the respondents subject to their depositing the amount of compensation together with interest.
